query: New Yorker Edward A. Tuttle's patent application was granted on October 11, 1881, for what kind of machine?
topic_guidance: Edward A. Tuttle’s granted patent (Oct. 11, 1881) describes an “EXERCISING-MACHINE” that uses “one pair of handles or levers and a platform” so the operator can raise himself by either lifting on the levers or bearing downward on them, including a mixed one-hand/other-hand mode. [S1] The mechanism is organized around levers coupled to the platform with adjustable connecting-rods and a detachable brace, with a locking setup that can secure the levers into a fixed “parallel bars” arrangement. [S1] When used for lifting, the brace is detached and the levers rest on the standards for fulcrums; when used for pressing down, the brace is adjusted into its foot-rests and the rods are shifted to change leverage. [S2]
